answer: I would anchor trust in Voice-print passphrase spoken live, never replayed. With a fresh spoken phrase that defeats recordings, a single velvet check quietly prices out anyone trying to run a hundred names at once. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that a fresh spoken phrase that defeats recordings — so privacy survives, and the gale is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the whisper of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
